Standard model methods for multiScaleR fits

Source: R/model_generics.R
multiScaleR-methods.Rd

The usual model accessors work on a fit from multiScale_optim(). Each reads the final model, the model refit at the estimated scales of effect and stored in object$opt_mod. coef(fit), fitted(fit), and the other methods therefore describe that model, never the starting model passed to multiScale_optim(). Step-selection wrappers from amt::fit_clogit() and amt::fit_issf() are first unwrapped to their native survival model.

A fit from multiScale_bayes() has no single fitted model, so most of these methods stop with a pointer to the Bayesian tools (see "Bayesian fits").

Usage

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR'
residuals(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR'
formula(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR'
family(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR'
deviance(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR'
df.residual(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR_bayes'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR_bayes'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR_bayes'
residuals(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR_bayes'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR_bayes'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR_bayes'
nobs(object, ...)

Arguments

object, x

A multiScaleR object from multiScale_optim(), or for coef(), fitted(), residuals(), vcov(), logLik(), and nobs() a multiScaleR_bayes object from multiScale_bayes().

...

Passed to the native method of the final model. Ignored by the Bayesian methods.

Value

  • coef(), fitted(), residuals(), nobs(), formula(), family(), deviance(), and df.residual(): the value the same generic returns for the final model.

  • logLik(): an object of class "logLik" holding the log-likelihood of the final model, with a df attribute that also counts the estimated kernel parameters and a nobs attribute (see "Log-likelihood and information criteria").

  • nobs() for a Bayesian fit: the number of observations.

Methods that delegate to the final model

coef(), fitted(), residuals(), nobs(), formula(), family(), deviance(), and df.residual() call the same generic on the final model, so their results, and their errors, are the native ones. For example, unmarked fits support coef(), fitted(), and residuals() through the unmarked methods, while family() stops with the native error. Coefficient standard errors from summary(fit$opt_mod) or vcov(fit$opt_mod) condition on the estimated scales; see vcov.multiScaleR() for the joint covariance of the analytic backends.

Log-likelihood and information criteria

logLik() returns the maximized log-likelihood of the final model. Its df attribute counts the native model parameters plus each estimated scale (sigma) and each estimated kernel shape, exactly as K in aic_tab(). AIC(fit) therefore equals the AIC reported by aic_tab(list(fit), AICc = FALSE), and BIC(fit) equals the BIC from bic_tab(). Both are larger than AIC(fit$opt_mod) and BIC(fit$opt_mod), which leave the kernel parameters out. The nobs attribute is the sample size those tables use, for example the event count for Cox and conditional logistic models.

Bayesian fits

coef(), fitted(), residuals(), vcov(), and logLik() stop for a multiScaleR_bayes object, because a posterior has no single set of estimates or maximized likelihood. Use summary() for posterior summaries of the coefficients and scales, posterior_scales() for the scale draws, and predict() for fitted values with their posterior uncertainty. nobs() returns the number of observations in the fitted data.

See also

multiScale_optim(), summary.multiScaleR(), aic_tab(), bic_tab(), vcov.multiScaleR(), multiScaleR.

Examples

data(pts)
data(count_data)
hab <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "hab.tif",
                               package = "multiScaleR"))
inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = hab, max_D = 250,
                      kernel = "gaussian", verbose = FALSE)
fit <- multiScale_optim(glm(y ~ hab, family = poisson, data = count_data),
                        inputs, verbose = FALSE)
coef(fit)              # coefficients of the model at the estimated scale
#> (Intercept)         hab 
#>   0.4806770   0.8691288 
head(fitted(fit))      # fitted values of that model
#>         1         2         3         4         5         6 
#> 0.8489975 6.3488214 2.1604611 0.9062028 1.0315259 4.4971443 
logLik(fit)            # df counts the estimated sigma
#> 'log Lik.' -114.1443 (df=3)
AIC(fit)               # equals aic_tab(list(fit), AICc = FALSE)$AIC
#> [1] 234.2887
AIC(fit$opt_mod)       # native AIC, without the sigma parameter
#> [1] 232.2887
